Surah 66 (At-Tahrim): It is Madani.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} This is a reproach from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) when he forbade himself his concubine Mariyah, or drinking honey, out of consideration for the feelings of some of his wives, in a well-known story. So Allah [Most High] revealed these verses. {O Prophet}: that is, O you whom Allah has blessed with prophethood, messengership and revelation. {Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?}: of the good things which Allah has bestowed upon you and your community. {Seeking to please your wives}: by that prohibition. {And Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful}: this is an explicit statement that Allah has forgiven His Messenger, lifted from him the blame, and shown him mercy.

{2} That prohibition which came from him became the cause for legislating a general ruling for the whole community, so Allah the Most High said: {Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths}: this is general to the oaths of all believers; that is, He has legislated and decreed that by which your oaths may be dissolved before breaking them, and by which they may be expiated after breaking them. This is as in His saying: {O you who believe, do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love transgressors...} until He said: {Its expiation is feeding ten needy persons with the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. But whoever does not find [the means], then fasting for three days. That is the expiation for your oaths when you have sworn}. So whoever forbids for himself something lawful, whether food, drink, a concubine, or swears an oath by Allah to do or not to do something, then breaks it and intends to break it, must perform this mentioned expiation. And His saying: {Allah is your Protector}; that is, the one who manages your affairs and nurtures you in the best way in matters of your religion and your worldly life, and in what averts evil from you; therefore He ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths so that your obligations may be cleared. {And He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise}: whose knowledge encompasses your outward and inward states, and who is All-Wise in all He has created and decreed; therefore He has legislated for you the rulings that He knows to be consistent with your interests and suited to your circumstances.

{3} His saying: {And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement}: Most of the exegetes said: it was Hafsah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her. The Prophet (ﷺ) confided a statement to her and commanded that she tell no one of it, but she related it to Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and Allah informed him of that news which she had spread. So he (ﷺ) acquainted her with some of what she had said and overlooked some of it, out of his generosity and forbearance (ﷺ). So she said to him: {Who told you this?}: the news that did not come out from us. {He said: I was informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware}: whom nothing is hidden, who knows the secret and what is more hidden.

{4} His saying: {If you two repent to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined}: the address is to the two noble wives, Hafsah and Aishah, may Allah be pleased with them, when they were the cause of the Prophet (ﷺ) forbidding upon himself what he loved. So Allah offered them repentance and reproached them for that, and informed them that your hearts had inclined; that is, they had turned and deviated from what they ought to have of piety and courtesy with the Messenger (ﷺ) and of honoring him, and that they should not trouble him. {But if you cooperate against him}; that is, if you help each other in what troubles him, and this matter continues from you. {Then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that are supporters}; that is, all of them are helpers and supporters of the Messenger. Whoever has these as his helpers is the one who is victorious, and whoever opposes him is forsaken. In this is the greatest virtue and honor for the Master of the messengers, in that the Creator made His noble self and His special creation helpers for this noble Messenger. And in it is a warning to the two noble wives that is not hidden.

{5} Then He also frightened them with a situation that is most difficult for women, namely divorce, which is the greatest thing for them, so He said: {Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you}; that is, do not raise yourselves against him, for if he divorced you the matter would not be difficult for him, and he would not be in need of you; he would find others, and Allah would replace them with wives better than you in religion and beauty. This is from the category of a conditional that has not occurred and whose occurrence is not necessary, for he did not divorce them; and had he divorced them, then the virtuous wives Allah mentioned would be these, combining Islam, which is upholding the outward legislations, and faith, which is upholding the inward legislations of beliefs and deeds of the heart, and devout obedience, which is persistence and continuance in obedience. {Repentant}: from what Allah dislikes, so He described them with upholding what Allah loves and repenting from what Allah dislikes. {Previously married and virgins}; that is, some of them are previously married and some are virgins, so that he (ﷺ) may have variety in what he loves. [And in this is evidence that Allah the Most High does not choose for His Messenger except the most perfect states and the highest matters; since Allah chose for His Messenger the continuation of his mentioned wives with him, it indicates that they are the best and most perfect of women.]

{6} That is: O you who have been blessed by God with faith! Fulfil its requirements and conditions. ﴿Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ described with these dreadful attributes. Protecting oneself means obliging oneself to carry out God's command, in compliance, and to avoid His prohibition, in abstention, and to repent of whatever angers God and makes punishment due. Protecting one's family and children means disciplining them, teaching them, and compelling them to obey God's command. A servant is not safe unless he does what God has commanded regarding himself and regarding those under his guardianship and authority, such as wives, children, and others under his care and management. God described the Fire with these attributes to deter His servants from being negligent in obeying Him. So He said: ﴿whose fuel is men and stones﴾, as He said elsewhere: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell; you will be its certain entrants﴾. ﴿Over it are angels, harsh and severe﴾; that is, their characters are coarse, and their rebuke is fierce. They terrify with their voices, distress with their appearance, and humiliate the people of the Fire by their strength, and they carry out God's command, which has decreed the punishment upon them and made severe retribution obligatory for them. ﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾. This also contains praise of the noble angels, their submission to God's command, and their obedience to Him in everything He commands them.

{7} That is: the people of the Fire will be rebuked on the Day of Resurrection with this rebuke, and it will be said to them: ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today﴾; that is, the time for making excuses has passed and its benefit has ceased, so nothing remains now but the recompense for deeds, while you had only sent forward disbelief in Allah, denial of His signs, and opposition to His messengers and His allies.

{8} God has commanded sincere repentance (al-tawbah al-nasuh) in this verse, and has promised for it the expiation of sins, entry into the Gardens, and success and salvation. This is on the day when the believers will strive forward on the Day of Resurrection by the light of their faith, walking by its radiance, and enjoying its spirit and ease. They will be fearful when the lights given to the hypocrites are extinguished, and they will ask God to perfect their light for them. God will answer their supplication and will bring them, by means of the light and certainty they possess, to the Gardens of bliss and the presence of the Generous Lord. All of this is among the effects of sincere repentance. By it is meant a comprehensive repentance encompassing all sins, which the servant makes a binding commitment to God, desiring by it nothing but the face of God and closeness to Him, and which he maintains throughout all his circumstances.

Allah commands His Prophet (ﷺ) to strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and to be harsh with them in that. This includes striving against them by establishing the proof against them, calling them with fair admonition, and refuting the various kinds of misguidance they hold to; and striving against them with weapons and fighting those who refuse to answer the call of Allah and submit to His judgment. For this one is to be struggled against and dealt with harshly. As for the first level, it is with that which is best.

The disbelievers and the hypocrites have a punishment in this world, through Allah's empowering His Messenger and his party over them and over their struggle against them, and the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter, ﴿and wretched is the destination﴾: the place to which every wretched, losing person will go.

These two examples which Allah has struck for the believers and the disbelievers are to make clear to them that the disbeliever's connection to the believer and his closeness to him does not benefit him at all, and that the believer's connection to the disbeliever does not harm him at all while he fulfills what is obligatory upon him. Thus there is in this an allusion and a warning to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) against disobedience, and that their connection to him (ﷺ) will not benefit them at all along with wrongdoing. So He said:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 66, verse 10–12:

{10} {God presents as an example for those who disbelieve the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants,} i.e., the two women were {under two of Our righteous servants}, namely Noah and Lot, peace be upon them, {but they betrayed them} in religion, in that they were not upon the religion of their husbands. This is the meaning of betrayal, not betrayal of lineage and marital bed, for indeed the wife of no prophet ever committed adultery, and God would never make the wife of any of His prophets an adulteress. {But they availed them nothing against God} i.e., Noah and Lot did not avail their wives {against God} in any way, {and it was said} to them both, {"Enter the Fire with those who enter."}

{11} {And God presents as an example for those who believe the wife of Pharaoh} and she is Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, may God be pleased with her, {when she said, "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people."} So God described her with faith and humble supplication to her Lord, and her request was the most sublime of aims: entry into Paradise and nearness to the Generous Lord. She asked that He save her from the trial of Pharaoh, his wicked deeds, and the trial of every wrongdoer. God answered her, and she lived in complete faith, perfect steadfastness, and deliverance from trials. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Many men have reached perfection, but among women none has reached perfection except Mary, daughter of Imran, and Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, and Khadijah, daughter of Khuwaylid. And the excellence of 'A'ishah over women is like the excellence of tharid over other food."

{12} And His saying: {and Mary, daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity} i.e., she preserved it and protected it from immorality, owing to the perfection of her piety, modesty, and purity. {So We breathed into it of Our Spirit} namely, Gabriel, peace be upon him, breathed into the opening of her garment, and his breath reached Mary, and from her came Jesus, peace be upon him, the noble Messenger and the great master. {And she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures} This is a description of her with knowledge and understanding, for belief in the words of God includes His religious and decreed words, and belief in His scriptures requires knowing that by which belief is attained, and this is not achieved except through knowledge and action. For this reason He said: {and she was among the devoutly obedient} i.e., those who persist in obeying God with fear and humility. This is a description of her with perfection of action, for she, may God be pleased with her, was a *siddiqah* (truthful one). And *siddiqiyyah* is the perfection of knowledge and action.

*Completed. And to God belongs all praise.*
